I traced this read-only at HEAD 2dd32236. Nothing was built, tested or run.

(1) The possible defect is REAL by reading. A Surface union is a union-of-parts region: it has `parts`, no faces, no filter and no cuts. Tapping a face inside one selects the union through `outermostUnion`, and the pattern tool then sets `surfacePatternPiece` to that union. `commitSurfacePattern` passes the union to `splitGrid`. `splitGrid` copies the parent's filter, add and cuts and never copies `parts`, so every cell resolves to zero faces. The preview's grid and its sliver verdict are both built from the single tapped face, so the confirm stays enabled and the empty cells are committed. Once committed, the cells are never hit, never drawn and never listed for the group. But every region is declared in `face_regions`, and core rejects any declared region that resolves to no faces, so a run would fail.

There is a second defect I did not expect, also by reading: the union-of-parts region itself goes out on the wire with no membership. Neither the wire map nor the bridge spec carries `parts`, and core does not accept that key. So any Surface union should make core refuse the run, whether or not it was patterned.

(2) All removal sites were re-verified. The line numbers are unchanged up to 2284; from the `handleTopologyPiecePick` guard onward they moved by +11. No source-pin test reads `WorkspacePlaceholder.swift` for any string being removed. The only tests touching the sheet model are three tests in `FaceRegionTests`. None of the removal sites is on the path that builds the run request, so a before/after stage-hash dump should show no change. His saved data was checked from snapshot S1-2026-10-02: 9 regions, each a single face with no filter, cuts or parts.

risks: Both defects are by reading only. No test was built or run, and I did not confirm core's refusal on a real job. The control tests above are what turn the reading into evidence.

The union-of-parts emission defect means 'combine, then pattern', and Surface unions in general, cannot be relied on for a run at all until it is fixed. A fix has to change the face_regions or region_ids emission, which the task lists as must-not-touch. His saved data has no unions, so his stage hashes would not move, but this still needs a ruling.

Moving Undo split or Dissolve onto a Surface union without going through resolvedLeaves would destroy the union's parts: revertSplit drops children(of:), which includes the parts, and Dissolve with members=[] gives no faces back.

A 'whole-region split' through the current Surface Pattern is not equivalent to the popover's. Surface frames and prices on one face (ProjectModel.swift:1621-1625, 1661-1666). On a filter-backed union with several faces, the other members would be cut by planes laid out for one face, and the sliver verdict would not count them.

The popover writes straight to project.faceRegions without sealUndoStep, and outside the Surface stage's revert-on-leave snapshot. Once the abilities move, they come under Surface's leave-without-save revert (ProjectModel.swift:1765-1795). That is a behaviour change worth stating in the handoff.

Memory notes that stage-job hash dumps can flap with hash-ordered state, yet dump_stage_hashes.sh unsets SWIFT_DETERMINISTIC_HASHING. If any hash moves, diff the key-sorted JSON before blaming the removal.

Is fixing the union-of-parts emission (no `parts` on the wire, so core sees an empty region) in scope for this task, given that face_regions / region_ids emission is must-not-touch? Or should it be a separate task with its own ruling?
Should FaceRegionSheetModel's pure pricing be kept, renamed, as the Surface whole-region split's model, so the three FaceRegionTests port across? Or should those tests be deleted along with the file?

Where should the Small-faces filter, with its size and radius sliders and the filter-backed Combine plus drift banner, live on the Surface stage? The Similar tool's ✓ union was removed by an explicit maintainer ruling (WorkspacePlaceholder.swift:7995-8005).
